text.p: England were reeling at 79 for eight on Friday on the second day of their four-day tour match against New Zealand A.

England, resuming at 30 for three and chasing a first innings target of 181, lost four wickets in the space of 36 balls in the first hour as the new ball pair of Geoff Allott and Heath Davis made swift inroads.
They were helped by a pitch offering inconsistent bounce and plenty of disconcerting lift.

Nasser Hussain edged the first ball of the day from left-armer Allott just short of Craig Spearman at first slip and England's troubles began after Hussain and Craig White had each picked up a boundary off Allott, through cover point and third man respectively.

White fended a short ball from Allott to Phil Chandler at short leg in the fifth over before Hussain survived a very confident appeal for a catch at the wicket off Davis, only to depart to the next ball.
He received an unplayable delivery that exploded off the pitch, clipped the shoulder of Hussain's bat and lobbed to Chris Harris at gully.
Hussain had grafted for 76 minutes for his 14 runs, faced 52 balls and managed just five scoring strokes.
Davis then had Robert Croft dropped by captain Darrin Murray above his head at second slip before the England player had scored.
The resulting two runs were all Croft managed as Davis got his revenge in his next over.
Croft drove at Davis and Matt Horne grasped a good low catch at third slip.
Two balls later Jack Russell speared a catch straight to Harris at gully. That gave Davis three wickets in 12 balls.
Ronnie Irani went on the offensive, lifting Allott for four to mid-wicket. Andrew Caddick hit Davis to the backward point boundary before being caught and bowled by Wiseman for six.
